newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Who silenced Winnie Mandela at New York rally?.
newsitem.headline: Who silenced Winnie Mandela at New York rally?.

text.p: Winnie Mandela, the ex-wife of South African president Nelson Mandela, was unusually silent on Thursday at a rally called by Louis Farrakhan, leader of the Nation of Islam in the United States.
A powerful speaker, Mandela's address at the rally was read by someone else and she said nothing at a news conference later at the United Nations.

Farrakhan said she was restricted from speaking by both the United States and the South African governments but U.S. State Department officials denied it. South African envoys were not immediately available for comment.
"We are appalled that she could come to the United States of America under the conditionality that she not utter one word to people who came to hear what she had to say," Farrakhan said.

"She has five days and I would hope that we could prevail upon the State Department and the upon the government of South Africa to let Winnie Mandela go free," he said, adding: "She is a heroine to all the females and males in America who watched her carry the movement while her husband was languishing in jail."

In both Washington and New York, State Department officials were adamanant in saying that there were no restrictions on her visa, either in New York or in Chicago where she is expected to travel shortly.
"We don't have a problem. Absolutely no restrictions were placed on her visa as regards public speaking," said one official.

Mandela has run into severe problems with her former husband's administration as well as his African National Congress. She has been accused of misusing funds and allegedly demanding bribes in exchange for help in getting government contracts but has not been charged officially.
